Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

[0] internal/common/config/config.go:124: The function docstring should document that old hash-suffixed ConfigMaps accumulate during the owner's lifetime, since Kubernetes garbage collection only fires when the owner is deleted. Each data change creates a new ConfigMap name (due to the hash suffix), but the previous ConfigMaps are not cleaned up.

Consider adding a note to the function docstring:

```go
// CreateImmutableConfigMap creates an immutable ConfigMap with a content-hash
// suffix appended to the base name. The hash ensures configuration changes
// result in new ConfigMap names, triggering pod restarts. It returns the
// actual name of the created ConfigMap (with hash suffix).
// 
// Note: Old ConfigMaps with the same baseName but different hash suffixes
// accumulate during the owner's lifetime since GC only removes them when the
// owner is deleted. Callers (reconcilers) should prune obsolete ConfigMaps
// after rolling updates complete to avoid unbounded growth.
```

This prevents operational surprises when owners with frequent config updates accumulate many orphaned ConfigMaps over time.

[1] internal/common/config/config.go:139: The hash encoding format is ambiguous for ConfigMap values containing embedded newlines. A single-entry ConfigMap with key `"key1"` and value `"x\nb=y"` produces the same hash as a two-entry ConfigMap with entries `key1="x"` and `b="y"`. This matters because OpenStack config values (e.g., full INI blobs) regularly contain newlines, making this a realistic collision rather than theoretical.

The docstring claims the format is "unambiguous" because "ConfigMap keys cannot contain '='", but that doesn't prevent ambiguity when values themselves contain `=` and newlines.

Use length-prefixed encoding to eliminate ambiguity:

```go
h := sha256.New()
for _, k := range keys {
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(h, "%d:%s=%d:%s\n", len(k), k, len(data[k]), data[k])
}
```

This makes each entry self-delimiting regardless of content.
